schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: THE SIEVE MESH THAT LETS OUT THE ROUTE, held as a machine so its determinism is measured apart from the device that dials the host. Five sieves — enabled, never_routed, serves_kind, keyed, addressed — assembled by cairn.tools.base.nest and shaken over the authored stacks (providers, models, combos, domains). A combo survives when every sieve passes; what survives is ordered cheapest-first for the resolver to dial. The mesh itself is pure: json, pathlib, the nest primitive, the address resolver, and the import sieve's phase_of — nothing that reaches an oracle.
why: THE CARVE-OUT WAS FORCED BY A MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-13 (ticket the-route-sieves-carve-out-of-inference-domain). The mesh was already import-pure; only its ADDRESS put it inside a component that dials the host. bin/cmd/determinism computes is_gate and llm-reach at COMPONENT granularity, so the mesh living beside domain.py and host.py — which reach the oracle — would make any gate import a violation. The fix is the one already applied in-house: the seam stays in the device, the gate berths as a held machine. The precedent is cairn/devices/intention_extractor/machines/judge/, carved out the same day for the same reason.
invoke: `from cairn.devices.inference_domain.machines.route import route` — `route.route(kind, model, domain=..., stacks=..., overlay=...)` returns `{survivors, gradation, findings}`. `route.load_stacks()` loads the four authored stacks; `route.load_overlay()` loads the instance-space hosts.json. `route.RouteRefused` carries `.findings` on refusal. The device holds it and imports it lazily in domain.py and host.py.
node_class: code-seam — the mesh is the code, one address. Held by cairn/devices/inference_domain at devices/<device>/machines/<name>/, the shape CLAUDE.md names for a device's held machines.
entry: CARVED OUT of cairn/devices/inference_domain/route.py on 2026-08-28 — a move, not a fresh build: the module, its four authored stacks, and its proof teeth came across whole. The import surface was already pure; only the address changed.
state_and_history: None of its own. The stacks are authored class-space files; the overlay is the device's instance-space. The mesh is a pure function of (stacks, overlay, request).
gates: Its import surface is measured by an AST tooth: the module may import json, pathlib, cairn.tools.base.nest, cairn.tools.base.address, cairn.tools.import_sieve.sieve — nothing that reaches an oracle. The stacks carry the ruled rows by content, not by file-existing. The nest is the general nest (cairn.tools.base.nest), not a private copy.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) this module importing anything beyond its pure dependencies — the carve-out is worth nothing if the import surface widens; (2) route.py gaining a direct oracle-reaching import at its new address — the determinism violation this move exists to prevent; (3) the stacks drifting from the ruled rows — file-exists teeth would stay green while content drifts; (4) a sieve that did not run appearing as passed rather than absent.
horizon: Valid while the sieve mesh stays pure. The gate conversion (inspect_* returning proof records with attendance) is the next step this carve-out enables.
how_it_learns: It doesn't — the mesh is a pure function of authored rules. What learns is the STACKS: a provider added, a model's serves list updated, a combo edited. The stacks are authored by Akien and carried in class-space.
traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured — sieves are measurements), Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics — the stacks carry rulings as rows, not comments), the carve-out ticket's own traces.
owner: the inference_domain device (a machine has users, and here it has exactly one holder).
proof: proofs/test_route.py — 16 teeth including the import-surface measurement that is this machine's reason to exist as a separate component.
provenance: Ticket the-route-sieves-carve-out-of-inference-domain, filed 2026-08-13 during the SAME PATTERN EVERYWHERE sweep. Built 2026-08-28.
learns: Yes; it learns routing decisions from measured provider costs, latency, and failure rates.
